newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling stable vs dlr in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling stable vs dlr in lacklustre trade.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling was stable against the dollar on Monday in lacklustre trading, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 55.32, unchanged against the dollar. Against the pound, the shilling was posted at 90.93 from 90.79.
Dealers said the market was extremely quiet, with most traders keeping flat positions from the weekend.
"Maybe the Christmas mood has set in. Dollar inflows have slowed down to a trickle, and there is no trade incentive from either side," one dealer said.
But some dealers said buying from oil importers could emerge this week. "In fact, the oil people were calling around today morning looking for indicative rates," one said.
Financial analysts expected market sentiment to remain in favour of the shilling at least in the short term, since there are no new factors in the horizon.
Dealers said the money market tightened slightly as one or two primary traders in the market were reluctant to go below 18 percent.
Overnight rates were quoted between 13-20 percent from above 10 percent on Friday.
